newsitem.title: USA: Superbowl loss deflates Boston stadium idea.
newsitem.headline: Superbowl loss deflates Boston stadium idea.

text.p: The New England Patriots' 35-21 loss to the Green Bay Packers in Sunday's Super Bowl quelled interest in building a stadium in South Boston, legislators said.

Although the proposal to build a 70,000-seat, privately financed stadium in South Boston had been rejected in recent years, the Patriots' play-off run re-energized stadium talk, to the point that Massachusetts Port Authority, which owns the land where the stadium would be built, approved a "term sheet," which could serve as a prelude to a lease for the structure.

But the Patriots' loss, coupled with the battling between owner Robert Kraft and coach Bill Parcells over his contract has soured the mood and galvanized stadium opponents, State House News Service reported.

House of Representative Speaker Thomas Finneran, D-Boston, threatened to rewrite the MassPort's charter if the agency followed through on plans to lease the land to the New England Patriots at below-market rates, the Boston Globe reported.
"My prediction is that it won't be built," Finneran told the newspaper's editors and reporters at a luncheon Thursday. "I don't think there is any support for this deal in the House or Senate."
Finneran conceded changing the authority's charter could affect its ability to sell bonds and its AA rating from Standard & Poor's.

S&P director Eddie Perez told the newspaper a change in the charter is "a concern...because opening Massport's charter could not only change its potential development deals, but also other activities that Massport might be involved in."
Neither Finneran, nor Perez, could be immediately reached for comment.
